skill.name: react-component

security_audit.summary: All static external command alerts are false positives caused by markdown code fences and inline React or TypeScript identifiers in SKILL.md. The network alerts are documentation reference links only, with no automated request or data transmission behavior. No prompt injection attempt or malicious semantic intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use `React.memo` for components receiving same props frequently
- Use `React.forwardRef` when ref forwarding is needed
- `useEffect`: For side-effects with proper cleanup functions
- Use `useCallback`/`useMemo` for expensive operations in lists
- All custom hooks must start with `use` prefix
- [ ] **TypeScript Props**: Exhaustive type definitions, no `any` types

content.value_statement: React component work often needs consistent structure, hooks, tests, stories, and accessibility checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward typed, testable React components.
actual_capabilities: Guides functional React component structure with explicit TypeScript props.
Recommends correct hook usage, dependency arrays, cleanup, and focused custom hooks.
Promotes composition patterns such as children props, render props, and limited HOCs.
Specifies test coverage using Jest or Vitest with React Testing Library.
Requests Storybook stories for default, loading, error, and variant states.
Applies accessibility, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, and i18n readiness guidance.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include runnable scripts or generated project files.
It is limited to React UI work and excludes backend logic or non-React frameworks.
It references APIs such as api.getAttendance as examples, not implemented services.
It depends on the host project having compatible testing, styling, and Storybook tooling.

use_cases.title: Create Reusable UI Components
use_cases.description: Build typed components with clear props, loading states, error states, and accessible interactions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Tests
use_cases.description: Plan render, interaction, loading, error, and accessibility tests for React components.

use_cases.title: Document Design System Variants
use_cases.description: Create Storybook coverage for component states, props, and visual variants.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React functional component for [purpose]. Include TypeScript props, loading and empty states, accessibility basics, and a short usage note.

prompt_templates.title: Interactive Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a form with validation and events.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a React form component for [workflow]. Define typed values, validation behavior, submit handling, error display, and React Testing Library test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Reusable Custom Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Extract shared state or data behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom hook for [data or behavior]. Include typed return values, loading and error states, retry behavior, cleanup rules, and component usage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Component System
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a composed component with documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a composed React component system for [feature]. Cover props design, subcomponents, performance choices, accessibility requirements, tests, and Storybook stories.

output_examples.input: Build a student KPI card with loading and error states.
output_examples.output: A plan for a typed KPI card component, state handling, accessibility labels, focused tests, and Storybook variants.

output_examples.input: Create a reusable attendance data hook.
output_examples.output: A custom hook design with typed data, loading, error, refetch behavior, dependency guidance, and retry expectations.

output_examples.input: Document a modal component for a design system.
output_examples.output: A Storybook-oriented outline covering default, open, loading, error, and keyboard navigation states.

best_practices: Define prop interfaces before implementation and keep components focused on one responsibility.
Include loading, error, empty, and success states for asynchronous UI flows.
Pair each component with interaction tests and Storybook variants.
anti_patterns: Do not use class components for new React component work.
Do not omit hook dependencies or cleanup for side effects.
Do not hardcode user-facing text when the project requires i18n readiness.

faq.question: Does this skill generate backend code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on React UI components, hooks, tests, and Storybook documentation.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance requires explicit TypeScript props and typed custom hook results.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for ARIA labels, keyboard support, and WCAG 2.1 AA considerations.

faq.question: Can it create tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It requests Jest or Vitest tests using React Testing Library.

faq.question: Does it require Storybook?
faq.answer: It recommends Storybook files when component documentation and variant coverage are useful.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: No. The skill is markdown guidance and only includes documentation links as references.
